speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Hold the linen while I pour, Alse. A poultice that is lukewarm might as well be a cold cloth.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: It steams through the holland, Mistress. He will feel it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Here, Master Shakespeare. Hold it by the corners till you can bear the heat, and then press it where the cellar is. Two nights, he said, and salt between.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It has the heat of a bakehouse floor. Two nights, salt water, and Tuesday at ten. Twelve pence when it is out. I did not pay him today.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Tuesday. Ten. Twelve pence. Mark me, I will have those three and not a fourth of your own adding. And you asked him whether a gathering gum could wait till Lent.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I asked. He said it could, and I could not. That was the whole of his argument, and it was enough.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The soft of the loaf is on the board. A penny, and still a full thumb short. I did not cut a crust. He was particular, you said.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No crust. I am not in the shrew. I am in the house. The sheet upstairs can wait. The jaw is too loud for it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then leave the lovers till your head is one size. The sixpence was Monday. Twelve pence is a tooth. I will not have them mixed.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They will not be mixed. The twelve is his, on the day. This is the first night of the two. If I am awake before light, that is the jaw's business.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I have left a saucer with a little wool and the last of the clove-oil by your inkhorn, if the bran cools before morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Thank you, Alse. The cloves have stopped answering. The wool can sit there. I am not writing over it.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Drink the salt and sit still while the bag is hot. When it cools, bring it down and I will heat it again. You went yourself. I did not have to send you. That is the one sensible thing in the day.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I went myself. Tomorrow I am a Roman at two, and I will be home when the money is done. Tonight the sheet stays shut.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The salt is in the cup by your hand. He said morning and night. This is the night.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Morning will be the same cup. I am not improving his orders.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Two nights, and then his window at ten. I will heat the bran again if you bring the bag down cool. I will not heat it a third time to be kind.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two is his number. I will not ask you for a third. The sheet stays shut, and the saucer can sit.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: The wool is dry enough to hold the oil. If it stains the horn, I will move the saucer in the morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Leave it. I am not writing. A stain on a horn I am not using is a small loss.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Small losses are how a week gets expensive. Twelve pence is the tooth. Threepence was your board. Sixpence was Monday. I can say all three without adding them.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Do not add them. I am going up while the bag is still hot. If I am walking at two in the morning, it is the jaw, and it is not a candle.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Then I will not set a fresh candle on the stair. The one in the socket can burn down.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Let it. He has had enough light for one day. Sit with the salt, Master Shakespeare, and then go up.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The salt, and then up. Tomorrow the Roman at two. Tonight nothing on the sheet.
